data.text: Authorization determines what an authenticated user can do. Hot Chocolate supports role-based policies, field-level authorization, and custom authorization handlers.
Use `[Authorize]` on query or mutation methods to restrict access to specific roles.

data.title: Role-Based Access

data.text: You can also protect individual fields on a type using `[Authorize]` on properties or methods.

data.title: Field Authorization

data.text: For complex rules, define authorization policies in Program.cs and reference them by name.

data.title: Custom Policy
Authorization Errors
data.text: When authorization fails, Hot Chocolate returns a standard error. Clients should handle 401/403 responses gracefully.

terms.definition: The process of determining what an authenticated user is allowed to do.
Authorization based on user roles like Admin, Editor, or Viewer.
A reusable set of authorization rules defined in Program.cs.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: [Authorize] restricts access to resolvers and fields
Roles are good for broad access levels
data.takeaway: Next, we'll integrate JWT tokens directly.
